blocks.content: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands (A&N Islands) form India's easternmost Union Territory — an archipelago of 836 islands, islets and rocky outcrops stretched across the Bay of Bengal like a broken necklace between Myanmar and Indonesia. Geography is one of the highest-yield areas for A&N-specific exam questions because the territory's strategic maritime location, seismic setting and island geomorphology are unique within India and are tested repeatedly in UPSC, APPSC-style, SSC and state recruitment papers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India is the seventh-largest country in the world, occupying 2.4% of the world's total land area.
The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes through 8 Indian states, dividing the country into almost two equal climatic zones.
The Indian Standard Meridian (82°30' E) passes through Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, and determines Indian Standard Time (GMT +5:30).
Indira Point, located in the Great Nicobar Island (6°45' N), is the southernmost point of the Indian territory.
The 10 Degree Channel separates the Andaman island group from the Nicobar island group in the Bay of Bengal.

blocks.content: The archipelago lies in the Bay of Bengal, roughly 1,255 km from Kolkata and about 1,190 km from Chennai, but only around 190 km from Indonesia's Aceh coast and about 45 km from Myanmar's Coco Islands at the nearest point — making the Nicobars geographically closer to Southeast Asia than to mainland India.

The islands stretch north–south for about 800 km between roughly 6°N and 14°N latitude, split into two main groups by the 10° Channel: the Andaman group in the north and the Nicobar group in the south. The 10° Channel is about 150 km wide and is a critical fact tested often — it separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar.
Of the 836 islands/islets, only about 38 are permanently inhabited; the rest remain uninhabited, many under strict tribal-reserve or forest protection.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The '10° Channel' and 'Great Channel' are two of the most frequently confused facts — 10° Channel divides Andaman from Nicobar; Great Channel divides Great Nicobar (India) from Sumatra (Indonesia). Indira Point, India's southernmost point, lies on Great Nicobar, close to the Great Channel.
India accounts for about 2.4 percent of the total geographical area of the world.

blocks.content: Geologically, the Andaman & Nicobar chain is the emergent, above-water portion of a submarine mountain range — an extension of the Arakan Yoma range of Myanmar that continues south through Sumatra as the Indonesian archipelago. This makes the islands part of the highly active boundary where the Indian Plate subducts beneath the Burma micro-plate along the Sunda Megathrust.

Because of this plate boundary, the islands lie in Seismic Zone V, the highest earthquake-hazard category in India's seismic zoning, and have experienced major tremors and the catastrophic 26 December 2004 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake (magnitude ~9.1) and the Indian Ocean tsunami that followed — one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history, which submerged parts of Indira Point and altered the coastline permanently.

The climate is tropical, humid, and equable due to maritime influence, with the South-West monsoon (May–September) and North-East monsoon (November–December) both bringing rain; the islands receive one of the earliest monsoon onsets in India (usually by mid-May, well before mainland Kerala).

items: Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram. (Does NOT pass through Odisha or Bihar).
The 82°30' E Standard Meridian passes through 5 states: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh.
Channels to remember: 8° Channel (Minicoy & Maldives), 9° Channel (Minicoy & Lakshadweep mainland), 10° Channel (Andaman & Nicobar).

items: 836 islands total; only ~38 inhabited; 3 districts (Nicobar, North & Middle Andaman, South Andaman); capital Port Blair.
10° Channel separates Andaman from Nicobar group; Great Channel separates Great Nicobar (India) from Sumatra (Indonesia).
Highest point: Saddle Peak (732 m, North Andaman). Highest in Nicobar group: Mount Thullier (642 m).
Southernmost point of India: Indira Point, Great Nicobar. Northernmost island: Landfall Island.
Barren Island = India's only active volcano; Narcondam = dormant volcanic island, home to endemic Narcondam Hornbill.
Seismic Zone V; the 2004 tsunami was triggered by the Sumatra-Andaman earthquake, one of the largest ever recorded.
